standard_prerequisites.name: Approximation and descent lemmas from the theory of limits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Limits, labels limits-lemma-approximate-given-relative-dimension (proof line 6402), limits-lemma-descend-finite-presentation and limits-lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation (proof lines 6406-6407), limits-lemma-limit-dimension (proof line 6410) and limits-lemma-descend-module-flat-finite-presentation (proof line 6412)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply a finitely presented closed subscheme of dimension below n containing the non flat locus, descend it to a stage together with its dimension bound and with the flatness of the module off it, which yields flatness in dimensions at least n at that stage.

core_obligations: Sheaf property: for an fpqc covering, pullback data and a point t, choose i and t_i over t, compare the non flat locus Z_i in the fibre over t_i with the non flat locus Z in the fibre over t via flat base change of the flat locus, and conclude that flatness in dimensions at least n holds over T by the dimension formula for fibres after base change (proof lines 6348-6368).

Reduce the limit preserving part to the case where the morphism is of finite presentation: after taking a directed limit, use the finite affine coverings of the affine stage and of X over an affine base to reduce first to S affine and then, via the equivalence with the disjoint union of the pieces, to f of finite presentation (proof lines 6370-6393).

Finish in the finite presentation case: let U be the open flat locus of F over T, whose complement Z has all fibres of dimension below n, then find a finitely presented closed subscheme Z' containing Z with all fibres of dimension below n and containing Z in its interior, descend Z' and the dimension bound to a stage, and use descent of flatness off Z'_i to conclude that at that stage the module is flat in dimensions at least n, using that the complement of Z' is quasi-compact because Z' -> X_T is of finite presentation (proof lines 6395-6417).
proof_roadmap: Sheaf property: compare the two non flat loci through flat base change and apply the fibre dimension formula (proof lines 6348-6368).
Reduce the limit preserving statement to a finite presentation morphism over an affine base (proof lines 6370-6393).
Approximate the non flat locus by a finitely presented closed subscheme of fibre dimension below n, descend it, and read flatness in dimensions at least n off its complement (proof lines 6395-6417).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the functor F_n of points where the module is flat in dimensions at least n on the fibres is an fpqc sheaf, and is limit preserving when the morphism is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation and the module is of finite presentation (statement lines 6336-6345, tag 05MV). The proof splits into a short sheaf argument comparing the two non flat loci through flat base change and a genuinely longer limit argument: it first reduces to a morphism of finite presentation over an affine base using finite affine coverings, and then approximates the non flat locus by a finitely presented closed subscheme whose fibres have dimension below n, descends it together with the dimension bound and with flatness off it, and uses quasi-compactness of the complement to conclude. The approximation and descent step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
